primary_task: Scan a named agent skill directory for security issues (static scan plus manual review) and produce the Skill Security Scan report with a safe/caution/do-not-install assessment.

requirements.name: uv
requirements.evidence: **Requires**: The `uv` CLI for python package management ... `uv run scripts/scan_skill.py <skill-directory>`
requirements.basis: "bash": "... install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads) ..." (uv is published on PyPI)

requirements.name: pypi.org (PEP 723 dependencies of scan_skill.py)
requirements.evidence: Check PEP 723 `dependencies` — are they legitimate, well-known packages?

requirements.name: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
requirements.basis: "read": "read files in the working directory; search them by name pattern or content (glob, grep)"; "bash": "run shell commands on Linux x86_64 ..."

requirements.name: docs.astral.sh
requirements.basis: "network access to hosts outside the egress allow-list ... other hosts are refused" (docs.astral.sh is in neither egress_allow nor egress_deny)

notes: uv is marked hard because the document says "Requires", yet the document also gives a fallback ("If the script fails, proceed with manual analysis using Grep patterns"), so even without uv the task could proceed. uv's install guide host (docs.astral.sh) is unknown, but uv is installable via pip from PyPI. Unknown: whether the scan_skill.py PEP 723 dependencies are all on PyPI (check the script header).
